audit.whatIsWrong: Early text called the lane hard-won without naming why Ahri is safe: Q is 970 range against every Vladimir tool at 600 or less.
audit.why: Ahri outranges Transfusion (600), Tides of Blood (600) and Hemoplague (625). Vladimir also pays his own health for Tides of Blood, so he bleeds himself down while poking.
audit.corrected: Poke free from Q range, punish the self-damage, and commit only with Sanguine Pool down.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes described Vladimir's scaling without the numbers that make the advice usable.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s — the whole matchup is that cooldown. Transfusion is free and drops to 4.6s, so chip trades are strictly bad for you.
audit.corrected: Anchor every commit to Pool's cooldown; buy Grievous Wounds by the second item.

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither the untargetable window nor the anti-heal requirement appeared anywhere in the text.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool grants 2 seconds of untargetability, which deletes a Charm-into-combo spent into it. Transfusion and Hemoplague both heal, and Hemoplague heals per champion hit, so Grievous Wounds decides extended fights.
audit.corrected: Bait Pool, count the 2 seconds, then Charm as he surfaces; build anti-heal before his sustain item comes online.
sources: brief missingInteractions rules untargetable-dodges-burst and needs-antiheal

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[0] credited Vladimir with 'passive HP regen'.
audit.why: Crimson Pact converts bonus health to AP and AP to health; it grants no regeneration. His sustain is Transfusion and Hemoplague.
audit.corrected: Survive to scaling with Transfusion and Crimson Pact's health-AP conversion.

audit.whatIsWrong: LEVEL CHART DISAGREEMENT: phases[3..6].side read Skill/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir while win[3..6] all read Ahri.
audit.why: Two layers rendered two different answers for four rows. packet.levelChart is all Ahri, the win rate is 50.64% for Ahri, and whys[5]/whys[6] both state Ahri's burst still outraces his healing. Content layer is the correct side.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side set to Ahri to match win[3..6]; phases[3].rating raised to 6/10 to match its neighbours.

edits.before: Vlad has no real burst or engage before he pools reliably and his Transfusion poke is weak this early, so you can charm-combo him down while he's still squishy and low on sustain.
edits.after: Sanguine Pool is 28 seconds at rank 1 and Transfusion barely stings this early, so bait the pool, count the cooldown out, and charm-combo him down while he is squishy and has no answer.

edits.before: Hemoplague doesn't add damage or CC by itself, just amplification, so your Spirit Rush combo still bursts him down before his healing and pool uptime can save him.
edits.after: Hemoplague amplifies and heals him per champion hit, but brings no CC — Spirit Rush lets you charm him out of the zone before the plague detonates and pays him back.

edits.before: Once Rod of Ages/Riftmaker starts giving him real sustain and tankiness, Pool becomes harder to punish and his Transfusion poke starts stinging more, but your burst rotation still edges out his sustain if you catch him with Pool down.
edits.after: Once Rod of Ages or Riftmaker gives him real sustain, Pool is down to 19-22 seconds and Transfusion heals more per cast — buy anti-heal at your second item and commit only after you have watched Pool go. Your burst still edges his healing in that window.

edits.before: A fully scaled Vladimir has strong sustain and Hemoplague can swing teamfights for his team, but your burst combo still kills him faster than he can heal it back provided you punish Pool's cooldown rather than dueling through it.
edits.after: Fully scaled Vladimir heals through chip and Hemoplague swings teamfights, so Grievous Wounds is mandatory and your commit waits on Pool's 16-second cooldown — charm him the instant it ends and he has nothing left to go untargetable with.

edits.before: Vladimir is at his weakest right now — no reliable engage, a long Sanguine Pool cooldown, and Transfusion damage that barely stings. Charm into full combo punishes him hard since he has no way to all-in back or escape cleanly if Pool is down. Push this advantage aggressively before his sustain kicks in, because this window closes fast.
edits.after: Vladimir is at his weakest right now — no engage, Sanguine Pool on 28 seconds at rank 1, and Transfusion barely stinging. Your Q outranges everything he owns, 970 to his 600, so poke for free and charm into full combo whenever Pool is down. He pays his own health for Tides of Blood, so his bar drops on its own — push before his sustain scales.

edits.before: At 6 his Hemoplague is a delayed amplification effect, not direct damage or CC, so it doesn't give him a real answer to your burst — your Spirit Rush combo still kills him before he can capitalize on the mark. Keep forcing all-ins here, especially when you can bait Pool early in the trade and punish the long cooldown that follows. This is still very much your matchup.
edits.after: At 6 Hemoplague only amplifies and heals him per champion hit — no damage up front and no CC, so it never interrupts your combo. The trap is dumping everything into Sanguine Pool: he is untargetable for two full seconds, so hold Charm and your last dash until he surfaces, then finish him. Bait the pool early in a trade and punish the 25-second cooldown behind it.

edits.before: Once Vladimir gets Rod of Ages or Riftmaker online his sustain and tankiness ramp up considerably, and Hemoplague becomes a real teamfight tool for his side, but your burst rotation continues to outrace his healing as long as you force fights around Pool's cooldown instead of grinding through an extended duel.
edits.after: Once Rod of Ages or Riftmaker is online his sustain and tankiness ramp hard and Hemoplague becomes a real teamfight tool, but your burst still outraces his healing with Grievous Wounds up — build anti-heal and force fights on Pool's cooldown rather than grinding an extended duel he wins by attrition.

edits.after: Bait Pool early, wait out the 2 seconds, then commit

edits.before: Survive to scaling using Transfusion and passive HP regen
edits.after: Survive to scaling on Transfusion and Crimson Pact stats

edits.before: Vladimir wins by landing Sanguine Pool, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Vladimir wins by pooling out your combo, healing it back through Transfusion, and outscaling you once his health-AP stacks.

edits.before: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Check it before every step-up. - R Spirit Rush (last dash) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Vladimir Sanguine Pool: matchup-defining — 28s at rank 1, 16s maxed, 2s untargetable. Bait it, count it, then commit. - Transfusion costs nothing and drops to 4.6s, so chip trades only feed him; go in once or not at all. - Anti-heal before your second item.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — charm Vladimir the second Sanguine Pool ends; he has no other escape, only a health bar he paid for.

edits.before: If Vladimir opens the score, reset expectations and respect Sanguine Pool doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through charm picks.
edits.after: If Vladimir opens the score he turns that gold into health and AP at once — stop dueling, farm with Q, buy Grievous Wounds early, and take him only on a landed charm with Pool down.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Vladimir's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, deny him levels: shove with Q, dash-flank other lanes, then come back and charm him off the wave — Vladimir behind never catches up.

edits.before: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Q out and back through where he steps for Transfusion — the return is true damage.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: Charm him as Sanguine Pool ends, never before — spending it into the 2-second untargetable window hands him a free reset and your whole combo.

edits.before: Vladimir whiffs Sanguine Pool and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Your passive heals at 9 minions — clear with Q and trade at full.

edits.before: That is Vladimir’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Keep one dash to leave the Hemoplague zone before it pops.

edits.before: The last dash is your life insurance — an Ahri who spends all three going in is an assassin's favorite story.
edits.after: A missed charm is 12 seconds, and Transfusion costs him nothing to heal the chip back — hold it for the pool's downtime.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: With Sanguine Pool up he simply deletes your commit for two seconds — check that 16-28s cooldown before you spend Charm.

edits.before: Track Vladimir’s Sanguine Pool: Untargetable dodge — bait it before you spend your kill window. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Sanguine Pool (28s at rank 1, 16s maxed): two seconds untargetable erases any combo spent into it. Bait, count, then commit.
